messages:
Monica (CS): Customer AstraHealth reports that their chat endpoint (psi-chat-13b-4bit) is ~25-40% slower after we switched them to the 4-bit quantized variant and they're seeing small quality regressions (more repetition). p95 jumped from ~120ms -> ~170-180ms in their traffic profile. This started after last night's rollout. Can eng take a look? Logs + repro below.

Devon (eng-runtime): Thanks Monica. Can you paste repro steps + one request id? Also need the model manifest and whether KV cache was enabled for their route.

Monica (CS): Repro curl:
```
curl -sS -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
 -H \"Authorization: Bearer $REDBEAR\" \
 -d '{"model":"psi-chat-13b-4bit","input":"Summarize: The patient notes...","max_tokens":256,"stream":false}'
```
Request id: req_20260318_8321
Config: kvcache.enabled=true, batch.max=8, calibration=auto
Attached perf snippet: FP16 (psi-chat-13b-fp16) p95 118ms, avg 92ms; 4bit p95 172ms, avg 140ms. Quality: repetition increase ~5% based on our eval runs.

Devon (eng-runtime): Got it. Quick glance at the runtime profiler for req_20260318_8321 shows: 
```
[profile] kernel_select: candidate=4bit_fast (quantized) score=0.87
[profile] kernel_select: fallback_kernel=fp16_ref reason=\"scale_overflow_at_layer_6\"
[profile] kvcache: miss_rate=0.62 warmup=false
[latency] total_ms=172 kernel_ms=145 memcpy_ms=18 others=9
```
That fallback to fp16_ref means we hit a slow, unoptimized fallback path that triggers extra conversions. Also high kvcache miss_rate -> more full-context passes which triggers calibration and kernel selection more often.

Ravi (eng-ml): Calibration detail: the `auto` calibration mode does on-the-fly per-layer scale recomputation the first N requests when context shapes change. For chat workloads with many short-turn requests and KV cache miss bursts, we repeatedly re-run per-layer calibration which is expensive and prevents kernel precompilation. In offline tests calibration + kernel-select overhead added ~40-60ms per request on short sequences.

Devon (eng-runtime): Short-term mitigations to propose: 
- Force the endpoint to use the FP16 variant: model=psi-chat-13b-fp16 (this bypasses quant kernel path)
- Set calibration=offline (precompute scales at deploy time)
- Disable per-request calibration with env var QUANT_CALIBRATION=disabled
- Reduce batch.max to 1 for lower tail latency
- Enable kvcache.prefetch=true to warm up the cache on session start
Can CS push these as temporary config changes for the customer?

Amanda (oncall): I'll open an incident INC-2026-43 and start a canary with the offline calibration patch on staging. Please add a minimal repro we can run on staging. Also recommend adding a quick Console metric tile for `quantization_fallback_rate`.

Monica (CS): I'll message the customer with this plan. Draft: "Thanks — we're investigating. Temporary options: 1) switch to FP16 model, 2) toggle calibration to offline/warmup, 3) lower batch size. We'll run a canary and update you in ~2h. Apologies for the regression. —Monica"

Ravi (eng-ml): Long-term: avoid runtime per-request calibration by default for chat. Proposal: model manifest flag `quant.calibration_mode` with options [offline, streaming-safe, disabled] and update kernel-selection to prefer precompiled kernels if calibration is disabled. I have a prototype PR to remove repeated per-request reductions; will link once tests finish.

Devon (eng-runtime): Action items:
- Devon: run nvprof / Nsight on the failing workload and attach flame graphs (ETA 3h)
- Ravi: run offline calibration PR on staging against the customer's trace (ETA 6h)
- Amanda: open INC-2026-43 and run canary (ETA 1h)
- Monica: confirm which temporary option the customer wants (FP16 vs offline calib) and communicate ETA

deploy-bot: canary deploy started: canary_id=canary-20260318-77 target=staging (rolling)

Monica (CS): Thanks team — please post updates here. :pray:
